newsitem.title: FRANCE: French troops back African peacekeepers in Bangui.
newsitem.headline: French troops back African peacekeepers in Bangui.

text.p: French forces in the Central African capital of Bangui intervened on Sunday to stop disaffected local troops from attacking African peacekeepers, a French general said.

Officials of the Central African Red Cross said the death toll in fighting between former mutineers and peacekeepers had risen to around 30. Around 70 people have been wounded in the fighting which began on Friday.

"As part of support for the African force, French forces in Bangui became involved as part of self-defence to put a stop to firing at Senegalese and Chadian positions," General Jean-Pierre Perez told La Chaine Info television.

Perez, commander of the French troops stationed in Bangui, said the Central African ex-mutineers had started firing mortars at Chadian and Senegalese positions on Sunday afternoon after a lull earlier in the day.
He did not say how many French troops were involved in the action in the former colony nor whether there were any casualties.
The French Defence Ministry said 1,650 French troops were stationed in Bangui under a bilateral accord.
Some reports in Bangui spoke of a French soldier among the injured.
The injured in the fighting include five French nationals who were hit on Saturday by two stray mortar bombs that fell on the French embassy compound.
The African peacekeeping force has been deployed since a January 25 peace deal that ended a series of mutinies.

That deal, brokered by Mali's respected former military leader Amadou Toumani Toure, included a plan to reintegrate the mutineers from the paramilitary gendarmerie into their units. But efforts to achieve this have failed.

Mutinies in April and May 1996 began as protests over pay but became a movement to topple President Ange-Felix Patasse, a northern civilian elected in 1993. The third mutiny began in November and degenerated into ethnic bloodshed.
French troops restored order after the last mutiny and then handed over to the peacekeepers. The African force includes soldiers from Burkina Faso, Chad, Gabon, Mali, Senegal and Togo.
